highlights_headline: SkiaSharp 4.156.0 strengthens platform support while removing allocation and lifetime pitfalls across managed and native code.
highlights_body: Apple deployment baselines advance, browser WebGPU builds move their C++ support into the packaged native archive, and Android continuous rendering follows the display clock. Linux HarfBuzz integration is more robust when applications also load system HarfBuzz.

bullets.detail: SKData creation from a C string no longer reads beyond the native buffer and writes directly into SKData.

bullets.lead: Front-buffered streams release their retained source
bullets.detail: Disposing a front-buffered managed stream now releases the wrapped stream instead of retaining it.

bullets.lead: Android texture rendering follows the display clock
bullets.detail: Automatic continuous frames for Android GL texture views are paced by display refresh callbacks, avoiding redraws driven by buffer-swap throughput while preserving explicit render requests.

bullets.lead: Linux HarfBuzz stays within the bundled library
bullets.detail: The Linux native library binds its internal HarfBuzz function calls locally, preventing conflicts with a system HarfBuzz library loaded by another framework such as GTK.

bullets.lead: Managed pixel copies avoid an intermediate allocation
bullets.detail: Valid managed pixel buffers can now be copied directly into raster images, reducing allocation overhead without changing validation behavior.
UTF-32 buffer encoding and feature-string conversion reuse stack or pooled storage, reducing transient allocations while preserving existing shaping and decoding behavior.

bullets.lead: Apple native package baselines are updated
bullets.detail: The native libraries now require macOS 11.0 and iOS, tvOS, and Mac Catalyst 14.0; applications targeting older operating-system versions must remain on an earlier SkiaSharp release.

bullets.lead: Browser WebGPU C++ support ships inside the native archive
bullets.detail: WebGPU-enabled browser applications no longer compile emdawnwebgpu C++ source during their final link, avoiding C++ flags on application C sources while retaining the required JavaScript glue.

contributor_summaries.VirgilMing: Linux HarfBuzz symbol binding and improved Blazor CPU sample test synchronization
contributor_summaries.ramezgerges: Bundled the emdawnwebgpu C++ support into the browser native archive
